claim: Capping the TOTAL number of novelty-substitution events per replicate at a fixed budget B (rather than gating each eligible repeat independently by probability nu) passes all six frozen criteria in at least 16 of 20 primary replicates at the smallest B that clears the hapax floor.
honesty_precommitment: If the calibrated B, expressed as an implied event rate (B / total eligible-repeat opportunities in the stream), lands close to the nu=0.1-0.2 range already tested in frequency-novelty-null and bigram-novelty-null, this result will be reported as NOT revealing a new lever -- a negative/uninformative finding about this specific reparameterization, not spun as progress. The two designs are mechanistically different (budget-capping front-loads all interventions into the earliest-occurring repeats and leaves the remainder of the stream untouched, versus nu-gating spreading interventions uniformly throughout) and that positional difference, not just the volume, is the actual thing being tested.
base_mechanism: identical to bigram-novelty-null: Naibbe cipher (voynich-units commit 956a7c4fc39981f4d116fa3f4edfccce6d065571) + identical boundary-coupling rule (beta=0.50 fixed) + identical bigram-conditional exhaustive substitution search (same ordering statistic, same sparse-context fallback). Only the novelty-triggering rule changes: from independent per-event probability nu to a hard total-event budget B.

representation.roundtrip_required: collapse(expand(atom)) == atom for every atomic_alphabet symbol

boundary_coupling.note: unchanged from all three prior designs; not re-tested

budget_capped_novelty_injection.eligibility: candidate already emitted and atomic length at least 2 (same trigger condition as all three prior designs)
budget_capped_novelty_injection.trigger_rule: deterministic, not probabilistic: if events_used_so_far < B, attempt substitution; otherwise leave the repeat unmutated (behaves as baseline for that token instance)
budget_capped_novelty_injection.events_used_definition: budget is consumed ONLY on a successful substitution (an unseen variant was actually found and applied) -- an eligible repeat where the search exhausts without finding an unseen variant does not consume budget and is not counted as an event
budget_capped_novelty_injection.replacement_distribution: identical to bigram-novelty-null: exhaustive search ordered by running bigram-conditional frequency (sparse-context fallback to unigram frequency below 20 observations), cold-start fallback to fixed cyclic order before 5 tokens emitted
budget_capped_novelty_injection.search_and_fallback: identical mechanics to bigram-novelty-null -- only the trigger condition (budget vs. probability) differs
budget_capped_novelty_injection.positional_consequence_disclosed: because eligible repeats are encountered in stream order and the budget is consumed greedily by the first B of them, EVERY substitution event under this design occurs in the earlier portion of the ~80,000-token stream; once the budget is exhausted, the remainder of the stream receives zero novelty injection regardless of how many further repeats occur. This is a real, disclosed structural difference from nu-gating (which spreads events uniformly throughout), not an oversight.

baseline.note: identical to boundary-state-null's baseline; not rerun, reused by reference

configurations.pilot_calibration_rule: B chosen by a self-consistency-only pilot (3 seeds, budget_novelty_only config, beta=0) sweeping candidate budgets {500,1000,2000,3000,4000,4500,5000,5500,6000}, targeting hapax_share_of_types in [0.65, 0.75], selecting the SMALLEST B that lands in-band. Coarse sweep: B<=4000 all undershoot (hapax 0.43-0.61); B=6000 overshoots into band from above (0.679). Fine sweep 4500-5500: 4500->0.629, 5000->0.647 (just below floor), 5500->0.663 (in-band). Frozen: B=5500, the smallest tested value that lands in-band. Out of ~74,000 eligible repeat opportunities in the stream, this is roughly a 7.4% intervention rate -- but concentrated entirely among the first 5,500 eligible repeats encountered in stream order, not spread across all ~74,000. H2 recorded during the pilot (not used to select B): notably, H2 rose monotonically with B across the whole coarse sweep (2.735 at B=500 to 2.966 at B=6000) -- i.e., MORE front-loaded volume made H2 WORSE, the opposite of a 'fewer interventions helps' story. Full pilot log in logs/2026-09-21-claude-budget-capped-novelty-selfreview.md.
